IR_MATCH_* family pending" on both m3/m4 -- parenthesized pattern-match-with-replacement-as-expression is simply not lowered yet (top-level statement form works fine, rung04's OTHER 4 witnesses prove it). Per THERE IS NO XFAIL, the absorb tool's auto xfail=True (banner " XFAIL") was hand-reverted in ALL.csv+ALL.sno+ALL.ref (xfail is computed from `orig_green` at absorb time, which is always false for a witness that documents a real unimplemented-feature gap -- the tool has no way to know the red is deliberate) so the ladder runner counts it as a genuine FAIL, not an excused XFAIL; class row filed to hq_P (own lane, lower_snobol4-scoped, not a shared-node defect) -- see FINDING-2026-09-04-seat07-rung04-parenthesized-replace-expression-unimplemented.md. column3: SPITBOL manual Ch14 "Program Statements" -- "Label field" p.176, "Goto field" pp.177-178 (unconditional/conditional/direct goto)
column8: seat07 2026-09-04: rung05 FORMS complete per pp.176-178 read in full this session. Minted goto_unconditional (p.177: transfer regardless of success/failure of the preceding statement, proven via a deliberately-failing bare pattern match 'abc' 'xyz' :(after) that still transfers), goto_success_only (p.177 :S(LOOP) form, S alone with no F: a failing predicate with no F clause simply falls through to the next line), goto_success_and_failure (p.177 :S(OK) F(NOGO) combined form, both directions exercised in one witness), goto_indirect_label (p.177 :($('VAR' N)), concatenates literal 'target' with N's value then indirects via $ to the computed label), goto_lowercase_sf (p.178: lower-case letters s and f may be used interchangeably with S and F, regardless of case-folding -- both directions), goto_absent_statement (p.178: the Goto field may appear on a line without any subject, pattern, and replacement, the absent SPITBOL statement is assumed to have succeeded -- proven with a bare :S(after) line alone, since only a TRUE assumed-success would take the S branch), and label_leading_digit (p.176: labels must begin with a letter or digit -- a digit-led label reached by fallthrough). All 8 forms (7 new + the pre-existing conditional_goto base, which already covers the F-only case :F(LABEL)) oracle-cut from sbl -bf, scrip --run cross-checked before absorbing, all GREEN (no compiler gap this rung), CSV origin doubling hand-fixed, verified via master_extract_origin. Deliberate exclusions: (1) direct Goto via CODE() (:<VAR>, pp.177-178) -- NOT this rung's scope, rung16 owns CODE() construction and cites this exact page range itself for the direct-Goto form; minting it here would require building CODE() out of order. (2) case-folding of labels (p.176) -- same rationale as rung01's exclusion: this project's oracle runs -f (folding OFF, matching SCRIP's case-sensitive design), so a folding witness would test the book default against an oracle configured to do the opposite. One hazard found and worked around, not a class row: referencing a digit-led label via a bare paren goto target (:(1start)) makes the oracle try to lex '1start' as a numeric literal, ERROR 231 'invalid numeric item', immediately followed by a SIGSEGV in the oracle's own error-recovery path (same hazard class as the rung04 FINDING's literal-subject-illegal crash) -- sidestepped by reaching the digit-led label via fallthrough instead of a goto reference, which cleanly isolates the label-field rule being tested (whether such a reference is ever valid SPITBOL is a separate, unanswered question, left for whoever revisits oracle-crash inputs). Regression floor (--to 10) reverified clean.

column3: SPITBOL manual Ch7 "Tables" pp.91-96
column8: seat03 2026-09-04: rung07 FORMS complete per pp.91-95 read in full this session (p.96 opens a new, unrelated section "The Name Operator" -- the unary . prefix -- excluded, not this rung's construct; the pp.91-96 REFERENCE citation is the chapter's own page range, not a claim every page in it is about TABLE). Minted numeric_subscript_key (p.91: a real number as table subscript, T[0.093]=6, proving subscripts may be any SPITBOL data type, not just integers/strings), missing_key_returns_null (p.91: referencing a subscript never stored merely returns the null string -- does NOT fail and does NOT add the entry -- direct semantic contrast with rung06's out_of_bounds_fails: arrays fail out-of-range, tables never do), unique_key_overwrites (p.92: repeated assignment to the same subscript always modifies the existing entry rather than creating a duplicate row -- proven by converting to array and walking every row: exactly 2 survive for 2 distinct keys despite 3 assignments), table_initial_size_and_value (p.92: the full TABLE(Arg1,Arg2,Arg3) form -- Arg1 a size hint only, never a limit, Arg2 SNOBOL-compat and ignored by SPITBOL, Arg3 sets the value returned by every entry not yet explicitly stored, book's own TABLE(100,,'STUFF') shape), convert_table_to_array (p.93: CONVERT(T,'ARRAY') produces an Nx2 array of [key,value] pairs for every non-null entry, ordered by time-of-entry, not sorted -- book's own ROSE/New Mexico example reproduced verbatim), convert_array_to_table (p.93: the inverse CONVERT(A,'TABLE') -- an Nx2 rectangular array's first column becomes subscripts, second becomes values), convert_empty_table_fails (p.95: "Conversion fails if the table is empty" -- CONVERT on a table with zero entries FAILS in the Goto field, a distinct table-specific failure path from rung06's array out-of-bounds fail), nested_table_value (p.93: "Other tables and arrays can even be used as subscripts or data items" -- a table stored as another table's VALUE, dereferenced through a chained subscript). All 8 oracle-cut from sbl -bf, scrip --run (m3) cross-checked before absorbing. Deliberate non-forms: duplicate VALUES across distinct keys (p.92 prose, "No ambiguity arises from duplicate values") is not a distinguishable code path, just ordinary value semantics; &DUMP=2 dumping array/table contents (p.94) is a keywords-rung (14) concern, not TABLE's own construct. util_build_master_suite.py's post-absorption verification reported these 8 families UNVERIFIED -- not a data problem: manually round-trip-verified byte-equal via master_extract_origin against both the pre-absorption loose pairs and the oracle refs (see session commands). Loose source pairs deleted by hand after manual verification. column8: seat03 2026-09-04 session3: rung08 FORMS complete per Ch8 pp.102-110 read in full this session (p.111 opens a new, unrelated section "Program-Defined Data Types" -- the DATA/CONVERT-to-data-type mechanism belongs to a later PENDING rung, not this one -- the pp.102-111 REFERENCE citation is the chapter's own page range, matching rung07's p.96 precedent). Minted null_default_return (p.103: "If no assignment occurs, the result is the null string" -- calling a function whose body never assigns to its own name), freturn_signals_failure (p.103: transferring to the special label FRETURN returns failure with no value -- the caller's own :S()/:F() on the call site observes it, distinct from a normal RETURN), local_var_saved_restored (p.104: DEFINE's post-paren local-variable list -- 'SHIFT(S,N)FRONT,REST' shape -- saves/restores a local on a pushdown stack across the call so a name collision with an outer variable of the same name cannot leak), dummy_arg_saved_restored (p.104: "SPITBOL automatically saves [dummy arguments'] values before assigning the actual arguments to them... restored to their original values" -- same save/restore mechanism as locals but for the argument names themselves, proven with a dummy arg name colliding with an unrelated outer variable), returns_pattern_for_match (p.104: "Any SPITBOL data type, including patterns, may be returned" -- the book's own BREAK1 function reproduced, used directly as a pattern in a match statement), used_in_replacement_field (p.104: "[a function's value may be used] in the subject, pattern, or replacement fields" -- the replacement-field case, a function call supplying the replacement text of an X PAT = REPL statement), function_as_argument (p.104: "a function may be used as the argument of another function" -- nested calls, ADD1(ADD1(5))), call_by_value_default (p.106: "Function calls in SPITBOL transmit the value of the argument... cannot be harmed by the function" -- the default, contrasted by the next form), call_by_name_swap (p.106-107: the book's own SWAP(.X,.Y) example verbatim -- the name operator lets a function reach into and mutate the caller's actual variables, the direct opposite of call_by_value_default), array_arg_implicit_reference (p.107: "If the argument is an array or table name... it points to the actual data object, which can be modified by the function" -- the FILL(A) example's point, proven with a BUMP function mutating an array element with no name operator needed, unlike plain string/number arguments), recursive_factorial (p.108: "any SPITBOL function can be used recursively if it is designed properly" -- the book's own FACT(N) worked example, structurally identical to an existing non-ladder DEFINE witness already in the master (family user_function), confirming this project's independent oracle-cut agrees). All 11 new forms oracle-cut from sbl -bf, scrip --run (m3) cross-checked before absorbing, all GREEN both modes -- no compiler gap this rung (contrast rung04). Deliberate non-forms: the INCLUDE control statement and code.spt (pp.106-107) are a file/toolchain mechanism (Ch14 territory), not a DEFINE syntax form; LOAD/UNLOAD external functions (p.110) are deferred to Ch19/Appendix F by the book itself and are a linkage feature, not a language construct this ladder tests; the indirect-goto-via-function capability mentioned in passing on p.104 ("functions may even be used in the Goto field" via the indirect reference operation) has no worked example in the text and is left for a future continuation rather than guessed at. util_build_master_suite.py's absorption verifier gave DIFFERENT verdicts across this session's two attempts on the SAME 11 families with the SAME inputs: the first attempt (pre-rebase clone) reported all 11 UNVERIFIED -- the pre-existing, already-diagnosed fam+"__"+basename lookup-key bug rung07's NOTE describes; that commit then hit a rebase conflict on ALL.xfail against concurrent upstream commits, so the rebase was aborted and corpus re-cloned fresh per THE LOOP's disposable-clone rule, and the identical oracle-cut witnesses were re-absorbed onto the freshly merged tree, where the SAME verifier reported all 11 cleanly VERIFIED. The bug is evidently intermittent/state-dependent, not a deterministic miss -- worth noting for whoever eventually fixes the tool (not this row). Manually round-trip-verified all 11 byte-equal via master_extract_origin against the pre-absorption loose pairs on the final tree regardless of the tool's own verdict, before hand-deleting them. Discriminating power spot-checked on call_by_name_swap against a hand-corrupted /tmp copy of its ref.
